title: Query Crash Signatures
description: Query for software crash and signal-death signatures across a workload prefix to catch silent failures, scoped by default to the active incident attempt window (or trailing duration_minutes around last_occurrence / incident attempt) to avoid expensive multi-day sweeps and log query rate-limiting. Covers Python-level crashes (Fatal Python error, Traceback) and process kills (SIGILL/SIGSEGV/SIGABRT/SIGBUS/SIGFPE, FailureSignalHandler). Note: `si_code=0` on a signal means SI_USER -- the signal was sent via kill() by another process, NOT raised by the CPU. To query across multi-day spans without clamping, pass full_window=true.
instruction: python3 tools/scripts/pull_and_format_logs.py --project_id=${project_id} --workload_name=${workload_name} --filter_extra="(\"Fatal Python error\" OR \"Traceback\" OR \"Segmentation fault\" OR \"SIGABRT\" OR \"SIGILL\" OR \"SIGSEGV\" OR \"SIGBUS\" OR \"SIGFPE\" OR \"FailureSignalHandler\" OR \"received by PID\" OR \"Out of memory\")" --output_file=${output_file} --deduplicate=true --start=${start} --end=${end} --last_occurrence=${last_occurrence} --duration_minutes=${duration_minutes} --coordinator_only=${coordinator_only} --full_window=${full_window} --limit=${limit}

output_file.description: Output path for the queried logs.

start.description: Window start (RFC3339). Scoped to incident attempt window.

last_occurrence.description: Incident or crash timestamp (RFC3339). When start is not set, queries a trailing window around this timestamp.

full_window.description: Explicitly allow multi-day sweeps without clamping to trailing duration_minutes.

limit.description: Log read limit. The script defaults to 100, which silently truncates a whole-window sweep.
